{"parentUuid":"88735d2f-e501-4431-9306-75a927405b82","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"mcp_instructions_delta","addedNames":["plugin:context7:context7","plugin:serena:serena"],"addedBlocks":["## plugin:context7:context7\nUse this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service -- even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. {"parentUuid":"0f638b83-c4a7-49eb-a6ec-c05454b77acd","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- empirical-probe-first: Probe ALL viable strategies in a multi-option ladder BEFORE committing to one. Use when a session-plan / decision-ADR / spec presents ≥3 strategy options (e.g. \"Strategy A1/A2/A3\" or \"alternative B/C/D\") and the recommended option's source-evidence may be stale. Outputs a probe matrix per strategy + commit decision with empirical citation. Pairs with `vendor-api-probe.sh` (deterministic detection layer; SessionStart hook) and `decompose-work` (deterministic-vs-LLM split per probe). Charter promotion target — codifies L-S32-1 doctrine surfaced at S32 Track A pivot (master-plan recommended A2 vnstock alternate; empirical probe rejected A1+A2; A3 SSI direct httpx adopted instead).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Read FIRST every session. | Long-lived; updated each session boundary |\n| `memory/agent-notes.md` | Learned rules from real experience (post-mortem / drift / user correction). Append-only mostly. | Long-lived |\n| `memory/decisions/` | Sequential ADRs (`NNN-<slug>.md`) + `_template.md` + `README.md` index. 12-field schema (Track 2). | Append-only; supersession via status field |\n| `memory/sessions/` | One file per session: `YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md`. What happened, decisions made, files touched. | Append-only |\n| `memory/observations/` | Subagent return artifacts (per Track 6 spec). Each subagent writes one observation file describing what it did. | Append; cleaned periodically by aggregator |\n| `memory/checkpoints/` | Session handoff state for self-reboot (Track 5). `latest.md` is canonical pointer; timestamped historical files retained. | Append + latest.md updated each checkpoint |\n| `memory/patterns-discovered/` | Pattern mining outputs (Track 0 — DONE) + ongoing pattern catalog. | Append; significant patterns promoted to constitution |\n| `memory/drift-logs/` | Drift-check (DR1-DR12) results; runs on hook + on-demand. | Time-series append |\n| `memory/post-mortems/` | After significant failure or thesis-revoked event: what failed, root cause, prevention rule. | Append |\n| `memory/thesis-log/` | Stock-domain thesis exploration entries. Read-only for IMPL sessions. | Append + revisited per calibration |\n| `memory/sync-tracker/` | Track 8a output: Confidence Score SQLite + weights.yaml + auto-rendered `_index.md`. | Live updated by hooks |\n| `memory/self-awareness/` | Track 9 output: model × effort × thinking profile cards + known-issues + best-practices. | Live updated by Stop-hook aggregator |\n| `memory/mistake-log.md` | Track 7 deliverable: structured failure catalog. What went wrong / Root cause / Prevention rule / Severity. | Append; pre-flight read by all agents |\n| `session-plans/pending/` | Plans authored, awaiting execution. Phase 0 plan lives here. | Move to `completed/` when done |\n| `session-plans/completed/` | Executed plans; archived for reference + retrospective input. | Append |\n| `quality-reports/{deterministic,probabilistic,drift-reports}/` | Tier-1/2/3 gate outputs (CLAUDE.md § Quality Gates). | Per-run files |\n| `ubiquitous-language/` | DDD glossary + domain-mapping + drift-log. Stockforge stock-domain vocabulary. | Append; canonical via `/drill-me` |\n| `calibration/` | Empirical hit-rate data per signal type. Confidence claims MUST trace here (CLAUDE.md hard rule). | Append per thesis post-mortem |\n| `research/` | Research notes from `research-scanner` subagent dispatches (e.g., reference-repo studies). | Append |\n\n---\n\n## Contract Rules (BINDING)\n\n1. **Constitution is immutable absent explicit human approval.** `Edit/Write` to `agent-workspace/constitution/**` is in `.claude/settings.json` deny list. Track 7 writes constitution drafts to `proposals/`; user explicit approve moves them.\n\n2. **`memory/decisions/` is append-mostly + supersession-status.** Don't delete decisions; mark `status: superseded-by-D-NNN` to revoke. Sequential numbering (`001`, `002`, ...) — don't reuse numbers.\n\n3. **`current-execution.md` is the routing source-of-truth.** No skill, agent, or command may hardcode phase paths or session paths from memory; resolve via this file. Stale paths in CLAUDE.md or skills = anti-pattern.\n\n4. **Never edit `obsidian-vault/raw/`.** Immutable. Vault writes only to `wiki/`. (Established in stockforge CLAUDE.md.)\n\n5. **Provenance is mandatory.** Every decision file references its source (human prompt / spec clause / drift detection / agent inference). Every thesis cites source + as-of date (I-S2). Every confidence claim cites historical hit rate (I-S20-equivalent).\n\n6. **Agents never `git commit` in this directory unless user explicitly requests.** Stage only.\n\n7. **`patterns-discovered/` artifacts are READ-ONLY for production code.** Patterns must be promoted to constitution / skills / hook scripts before becoming binding. (Otherwise they're informal notes, not contracts.)\n\n---\n\n## Reading Priority for Agent\n\nPer `agent-workspace/constitution/autonomous-protocol.md` (Track 7) and stockforge `CLAUDE.md` § Session Protocol:\n\n1. **`memory/current-execution.md`** — first; resolve active track\n2. **`memory/project.md`** — project state\n3. **`memory/checkpoints/latest.md`** if a recent checkpoint exists (within last 24h) — resume context\n4. **`memory/agent-notes.md`** — learned rules\n5. **`memory/mistake-log.md`** — pre-flight failure catalog\n6. **Last 3 files in `memory/sessions/`** — recent context\n7. **`session-plans/pending/<active-plan>.md`** — current plan\n8. **Relevant constitution files** as task demands (don't load all every session)\n9. **Relevant skills + agents + commands** as task demands\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns to Avoid\n\n(From `memory/patterns-discovered/SYNTHESIS.md` § 6, full catalog 23 items. Highest-priority for this directory:)\n\n- **AP-1 Same-agent self-review** — never review your own implementation; dispatch fresh-context verifier\n- **AP-2 Self-track wind-down** — `.transcript-tokens` real-transcript is authoritative, not LLM self-track\n- **AP-5 Charter-coherence defer overriding user-CRITICAL** — re-read all `user_prompt/*` at every phase entry; never silently defer USER-CRITICAL\n- **AP-7 Performative SC ticking** — defer with explicit prerequisites > fire vacuous proposals\n- **AP-8 Pre-staged work causing checkpoint drift** — update `current-execution.md` immediately on task complete, not session-end\n- **AP-17 Identity drift** — stockforge is AI-first VN stock advisory; not generic financial framework (see `constitution/identity-scope.md` once Track 7 ships)\n- **AP-23 Continuous LLM-Guardian** — deterministic hooks = Guardian; LLM Guardian only at session-end aggregation\n\n---\n\n## Connection to human-workspace/\n\nThis directory is the agent's domain. Human's domain is `human-workspace/`. The two communicate through:\n- Human → Agent: `human-workspace/user_prompt/`, `human-workspace/decisions/`\n- Agent → Human: `human-workspace/notifications/`, `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/`\n- Bidirectional: `human-workspace/q-and-a/answered/` — agent writes pending; either human or agent (per Auto-mv rule below) moves resolved bundles to answered/\n- Audit trail: this directory's `memory/decisions/` references `human-workspace/` source files via path pointers\n\n**Auto-mv rule (HH-E.2 — D-031 ratification, 2026-05-05)**: Agent MAY mv a bundle from `q-and-a/pending/` to `q-and-a/answered/` IFF ALL of the following hold:\n\n1. **Frontmatter signal**: bundle frontmatter `status:` field value starts with one of: `answered-`, `closed-`, `resolved-`. Examples already in repo: `answered-via-chat`, `answered-via-AskUserQuestion`, `answered-2026-05-04-via-chat`. Detection is deterministic (head -20 of file + grep `^status:`).\n2. **No human-veto signal**: bundle frontmatter has NO `wait_until:` ISO-8601 timestamp greater than current epoch — if present, agent MUST defer mv until that timestamp passes. Allows human to override auto-mv per-bundle without contract amendment.\n3. **No global pause**: file `human-workspace/q-and-a/.auto-mv-paused` does NOT exist — global kill switch for the auto-mv mechanism (single empty file presence pauses all auto-mv).\n4. **Hook validation**: the mv is performed by `scripts/hooks/qa-pending-auto-mover.sh` (Stop hook). Direct manual `mv` invocation by agent (e.g. via Bash tool) is STILL forbidden — only the validated hook path is authorized.\n\nAgent never writes to `human-workspace/` outside the designated `q-and-a/pending/` write channel + the auto-mv rule above + `notifications/` write channel (existing).\n","contentDiffersFromDisk":false},"displayPath":"agent-workspace\\CLAUDE.md"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"0c410d43-da65-422d-997d-22dd03f0f141","timestamp":"2026-05-09T12:02:38.665Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"142a2b14-79c6-486b-8a85-0887f39d14e4","version":"2.1.126","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"ecc14aac-06e4-4cb3-9218-bc1674f4bc24","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"4a3ba620-13d8-46e1-aaaa-52b8a48eb91a","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_01SPTy86Px7W8MPXvT5jTFmD","content":[{"type":"tool_reference","tool_name":"TaskCreate"},{"type":"tool_reference","tool_name":"TaskList"},{"type":"tool_reference","tool_name":"TaskUpdate"}]}]},"uuid":"26745838-54cc-4338-aba7-afbb3138d952","timestamp":"2026-05-09T12:03:29.521Z","toolUseResult":{"matches":["TaskCreate","TaskList","TaskUpdate"],"query":"select:TaskCreate,TaskList,TaskUpdate","total_deferred_tools":76},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"ecc14aac-06e4-4cb3-9218-bc1674f4bc24","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"142a2b14-79c6-486b-8a85-0887f39d14e4","version":"2.1.126","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"b4421f4a-e118-40b0-a581-cba5b55e439e","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"4a3ba620-13d8-46e1-aaaa-52b8a48eb91a","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01E2Y5L2iLM6LUTMMhrrt6DF","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t---\n2\tspec_id: SPEC-2026-04-23-005\n3\ttier: 2\n4\tstatus: approved\n5\tversion: 1.0\n6\tcreated: 2026-04-23\n7\tauthors: [project-owner]\n8\tbounded_contexts: [Analysis, Calibration, Market Data]\n9\trelated_specs: [SPEC-2026-04-23-T1-001, SPEC-2026-04-23-004]\n10\tubiquitous_language_terms: [Outer Loop, Editable Asset, Scalar Metric, Eval Set, Goodhart's Law, Ratchet, Simplicity Criterion, Meta-Optimization, Walk-Forward]\n11\t---\n12\t\n13\t# SPEC: Karpathy Outer Loop — Pipeline Self-Optimization (Year 2)\n14\t\n15\t> Applies the Karpathy autoresearch pattern to optimize signal weights, prompts, and rules over time.\n16\t> **This spec activates in Year 2.** Year 1 is calibration-data-accumulation; without sufficient data, outer loop has nothing to optimize against.\n17\t\n18\t---\n19\t\n20\t# PART A — BUSINESS SPECIFICATION\n21\t\n22\t## A.1 Context\n23\t\n24\tKarpathy's autoresearch loop: LLM agent edits an `editable_asset` repeatedly, each edit evaluated by a `scalar_metric`, within a `time_boxed_cycle`. Best results kept (ratchet), simpler solutions preferred (simplicity criterion).\n25\t\n26\tApplied to StockForge: **we don't optimize investment decisions directly** (that's Goodhart trap — LLM would learn to hack whatever metric we use). We optimize the **pipeline** that produces investment theses.\n27\t\n28\t**Editable assets**:\n29\t- Signal weights in confluence engine\n30\t- Prompt templates for perspective agents\n31\t- Pump phase classifier thresholds\n32\t- KOL credibility formula parameters\n33\t- Narrative phase transition rules\n34\t- Screening rules in watchlist\n35\t\n36\t**Scalar metrics** (on HOLD-OUT set, not used for tuning):\n37\t- Thesis hit rate (primary)\n38\t- Alert precision/recall\n39\t- Pump detection precision/recall\n40\t- KOL calibration CI width\n41\t\n42\t**Time-boxed cycle**: each \"experiment\" = re-run pipeline on historical period + measure metric, ~1-2 hours.\n43\t\n44\t## A.2 Why Year 2 Activation\n45\t\n46\tKarpathy loop requires **evaluation data**. StockForge generates evaluation data through:\n47\t- Thesis outcomes (3-12 month review cycle)\n48\t- KOL recommendation outcomes (1-12 month cycle)\n49\t- Pump detection outcomes (30-90 days post-detection)\n50\t- Narrative phase predictions vs actual phase evolution\n51\t\n52\t**Minimum eval set sizes before outer loop meaningful**:\n53\t- 100+ completed thesis with outcomes\n54\t- 500+ KOL recommendations with outcomes\n55\t- 20+ labeled historical pumps with outcomes\n56\t- 10+ narratives through full lifecycle\n57\t\n58\tThese take ~12-18 months to accumulate. Running outer loop with insufficient data = overfit to noise, worse than doing nothing.\n59\t\n60\t## A.3 The Goodhart Problem\n61\t\n62\tThe #1 risk: outer loop optimizes for the metric, not for real-world value. Mitigations:\n63\t\n64\t**M-1 Hold-Out Test Set** — 30% of evaluation data never seen by outer loop. Final metric always computed on hold-out. If training metric improves but hold-out degrades: reject.\n65\t\n66\t**M-2 Multi-Metric Composite** — never optimize single metric. Composite of thesis_hit_rate + alert_precision + calibration_accuracy + simplicity_penalty.\n67\t\n68\t**M-3 Simplicity Ratchet** — if edit adds complexity (more rules, more parameters, longer prompt) but improves metric marginally (<5% lift), reject.\n69\t\n70\t**M-4 Walk-Forward Validation** — each proposed change tested on 3 non-overlapping historical windows. Must improve in ≥2 of 3 to be accepted.\n71\t\n72\t**M-5 Human Review of Proposed Changes** — outer loop proposes; human approves before production. Not autonomous in year 2.\n73\t\n74\t**M-6 Eval Set Rotation** — eval set refreshes quarterly (new data added, oldest retired). Prevents pipeline from memorizing specific eval items.\n75\t\n76\t## A.4 Three Loops Recap\n77\t\n78\t**Outer loop (this spec, weekly cycle, Year 2+)** — meta-optimization: edit pipeline params + prompts + rules\n79\t\n80\t**Middle loop (continuous, Phase 1+)** — ingestion: hourly news, daily KOL, scheduled reviews, live data\n81\t\n82\t**Inner loop (per-query, Phase 1+)** — thesis validation: ticker → 6 perspectives → synthesis\n83\t\n84\tEach loop has different cadence, different editable assets, different metrics.\n85\t\n86\t## A.5 Core Use Cases\n87\t\n88\t**UC-1 Weekly Optimization Run** — Every Sunday: outer loop picks one editable asset from candidate list, proposes N variations, runs each through eval pipeline, ranks by composite metric, produces report.\n89\t\n90\t**UC-2 Human Review & Accept** — User reviews weekly report. Approves, rejects, or requests modification. Approved changes go to production next week.\n91\t\n92\t**UC-3 Regression Alert** — If a change in production causes metric to drop >20% over 4 weeks, auto-rollback to prior version + flag for investigation.\n93\t\n94\t**UC-4 Proposal Archive** — All proposed changes (accepted or rejected) archived with full rationale + results. Pattern: what tends to work, what tends to fail.\n95\t\n96\t**UC-5 Manual Experiment Request** — User can propose specific experiment (\"try reducing KOL weight 20%\"), outer loop runs it through same eval pipeline.\n97\t\n98\t## A.6 Business Rules\n99\t\n100\t**BR-1 Never Auto-Deploy** — outer loop PROPOSES, human ACCEPTS. Year 2 at minimum. Maybe never fully autonomous.\n101\t\n102\t**BR-2 Eval Set Never Used for Training** — strict separation. Eval set lives in `eval-sets/`; training data for prompt refinement lives elsewhere.\n103\t\n104\t**BR-3 Multi-Metric Composite** — no single-metric optimization. Composite defined in `configs/outer-loop-metrics.yaml`.\n105\t\n106\t**BR-4 Simplicity Preferred** — complexity penalty in composite. New rule adds score iff |improvement| > complexity_cost.\n107\t\n108\t**BR-5 Walk-Forward Mandatory** — propose change → test on 3 non-overlapping windows → accept if 2+ improve.\n109\t\n110\t**BR-6 Rollback Trigger Automated** — metric drops >20% in 4 weeks of production = automatic revert to previous version, manual re-review required.\n111\t\n112\t**BR-7 Changes Versioned** — every pipeline version is a git tag. Rollback = git checkout.\n113\t\n114\t**BR-8 Proposals Limited Per Week** — max 3 proposals per week to prevent noise. Forces thoughtful selection.\n115\t\n116\t**BR-9 Prompt Changes Human-Reviewed First** — no automated prompt editing in year 2. All prompt changes reviewed line-by-line before testing.\n117\t\n118\t**BR-10 Minimum Eval Set Enforced** — outer loop refuses to run if eval set below minimums (see A.2).\n119\t\n120\t## A.7 Success Criteria (Year 2)\n121\t\n122\t**Month 15** (activation + 3 months):\n123\t- Outer loop runs weekly, produces reports\n124\t- ≥5 proposals reviewed, ≥2 accepted\n125\t- Documented cases: metric improvement from specific changes\n126\t\n127\t**Month 18**:\n128\t- Accepted changes show compounding improvement (metric lift from baseline)\n129\t- No auto-rollback triggered (changes were sound)\n130\t- Human review time <30 min/week\n131\t\n132\t**Month 24**:\n133\t- Outer loop has produced ≥20 accepted changes\n134\t- Pipeline metric improved ≥30% vs baseline\n135\t- Changes in \"pattern library\" (what kinds of changes work)\n136\t\n137\t**Qualitative**:\n138\t- I trust the proposals enough that review feels valuable, not performative\n139\t- Outer loop caught at least one case where my intuition was wrong\n140\t- Pipeline demonstrably smarter than when we started\n141\t\n142\t## A.8 Out of Scope\n143\t\n144\t- Autonomous code changes (outer loop proposes to config + prompts, not Python code)\n145\t- Optimizing individual perspective prompts (BR-9 restriction)\n146\t- Year 1 activation (insufficient data)\n147\t- Multi-user tenancy (single user Year 2)\n148\t\n149\t---\n150\t\n151\t# PART B — AGENT CONTRACT\n152\t\n153\t## B.1 Editable Asset Registry\n154\t\n155\t```yaml\n156\t# configs/outer-loop/editable-assets.yaml\n157\t\n158\teditable_assets:\n159\t  - id: confluence_weights\n160\t    path: configs/signals/confluence-weights.yaml\n161\t    description: How much each tier contributes to confluence score\n162\t    mutation_types: [numeric_range, numeric_relative]\n163\t    safety: high  # changes immediately affect alerts\n164\t\n165\t  - id: pump_classifier_thresholds\n166\t    path: configs/signals/pump-classifier.yaml\n167\t    description: Thresholds for pump phase classification\n168\t    mutation_types: [numeric_range]\n169\t    safety: high\n170\t\n171\t  - id: kol_credibility_formula\n172\t    path: configs/calibration/kol-credibility.yaml\n173\t    description: Bayesian prior + decay + sector weighting\n174\t    mutation_types: [numeric_range, formula_variant]\n175\t    safety: medium  # affects scoring but calibration is statistical\n176\t\n177\t  - id: narrative_phase_thresholds\n178\t    path: configs/signals/narrative-phases.yaml\n179\t    description: Thresholds for INCUBATION → EMERGING etc transitions\n180\t    mutation_types: [numeric_range]\n181\t    safety: medium\n182\t\n183\t  - id: screening_rules\n184\t    path: configs/screeners/*.yaml\n185\t    description: Watchlist screening rule variants\n186\t    mutation_types: [rule_addition, rule_removal, threshold_change]\n187\t    safety: low  # easy to revert\n188\t\n189\t  - id: synthesizer_prompt\n190\t    path: prompts/analysis/synthesizer.md\n191\t    description: System prompt for synthesizer\n192\t    mutation_types: [prompt_variant]\n193\t    safety: high  # affects all thesis output\n194\t    human_review_required: line_by_line\n195\t\n196\t  - id: perspective_prompts\n197\t    path: prompts/analysis/perspectives/*.md\n198\t    description: System prompts for 6 perspective agents\n199\t    mutation_types: [prompt_variant]\n200\t    safety: high\n201\t    human_review_required: line_by_line\n202\t```\n203\t\n204\t## B.2 Metrics Definition\n205\t\n206\t```yaml\n207\t# configs/outer-loop/metrics.yaml\n208\t\n209\tcomposite_metric:\n210\t  weights:\n211\t    thesis_hit_rate: 0.35         # primary\n212\t    thesis_excess_return: 0.20    # beats benchmark\n213\t    alert_precision: 0.15         # not crying wolf\n214\t    alert_recall: 0.10            # not missing opportunities\n215\t    pump_detection_f1: 0.10\n216\t    kol_calibration_convergence: 0.05\n217\t    simplicity_penalty: -0.05     # subtracted\n218\t\n219\t  normalization:\n220\t    # Each sub-metric normalized to [0, 1] based on historical distribution\n221\t\n222\t  simplicity_penalty:\n223\t    formula: |\n224\t      lines_of_rules_added * 0.01\n225\t      + prompt_tokens_added * 0.001\n226\t      + new_parameters * 0.05\n227\t\n228\tmetric_calculation:\n229\t  eval_periods:\n230\t    - start: 2023-01-01\n231\t      end: 2023-06-30\n232\t    - start: 2023-07-01\n233\t      end: 2023-12-31\n234\t    - start: 2024-01-01\n235\t      end: 2024-06-30\n236\t    - start: 2024-07-01\n237\t      end: 2024-12-31\n238\t\n239\t  min_thesis_per_period: 20       # won't run if fewer\n240\t  min_kol_recs_per_period: 100\n241\t  min_pump_cases_per_period: 5\n242\t```\n243\t\n244\t## B.3 Core Use Cases\n245\t\n246\t### UC-1: Weekly Optimization Run\n247\t\n248\t```python\n249\t# apps/analyst-agents/outer_loop/weekly_runner.py\n250\t\n251\tclass WeeklyOptimizationRunner:\n252\t    \"\"\"Every Sunday: pick candidate → generate mutations → evaluate → report.\"\"\"\n253\t\n254\t    async def execute(self) -> OptimizationReport:\n255\t        # Step 0: Check minimum eval set sizes\n256\t        if not await self._eval_set_minimums_met():\n257\t            return OptimizationReport(status=SKIPPED, reason=\"insufficient_eval_data\")\n258\t\n259\t        # Step 1: Pick candidate editable asset (LLM-assisted)\n260\t        candidates = await self.asset_registry.get_candidates()\n261\t        # Prioritize: assets not recently modified, assets where metric drift observed\n262\t        candidate = await self.candidate_selector.select(candidates, self.recent_history)\n263\t\n264\t        # Step 2: Generate mutations (3-5 variants)\n265\t        mutations = await self.mutation_generator.generate(\n266\t            asset=candidate,\n267\t            n_variants=4,\n268\t            constraint=candidate.safety_level,\n269\t        )\n270\t\n271\t        # Step 3: Run each mutation through eval pipeline (walk-forward)\n272\t        results = []\n273\t        for mutation in [current_baseline] + mutations:\n274\t            for eval_period in self.config.eval_periods:\n275\t                result = await self.eval_runner.run(mutation, eval_period)\n276\t                results.append((mutation, eval_period, result))\n277\t\n278\t        # Step 4: Aggregate walk-forward scores\n279\t        scores_by_mutation = {}\n280\t        for mutation, period, result in results:\n281\t            scores_by_mutation.setdefault(mutation.id, []).append(result)\n282\t\n283\t        walk_forward_pass = []\n284\t        for mut_id, period_results in scores_by_mutation.items():\n285\t            # Must improve in ≥2 of 3 periods\n286\t            baseline = scores_by_mutation[CURRENT_BASELINE_ID]\n287\t            improvements = sum(\n288\t                1 for mut_res, base_res in zip(period_results, baseline)\n289\t                if mut_res.composite > base_res.composite\n290\t            )\n291\t            if improvements >= 2 and mut_id != CURRENT_BASELINE_ID:\n292\t                walk_forward_pass.append(mut_id)\n293\t\n294\t        # Step 5: Apply simplicity ratchet\n295\t        ratchet_pass = []\n296\t        for mut_id in walk_forward_pass:\n297\t            mutation = next(m for m in mutations if m.id == mut_id)\n298\t            if mutation.complexity_delta < 0 or (\n299\t                self._avg_improvement(mut_id) > mutation.complexity_delta * 0.05\n300\t            ):\n301\t                ratchet_pass.append(mut_id)\n302\t\n303\t        # Step 6: Generate report\n304\t        report = OptimizationReport(\n305\t            week=self.current_week,\n306\t            candidate_asset=candidate.id,\n307\t            baseline_score=self._score(CURRENT_BASELINE_ID),\n308\t            mutations_tested=len(mutations),\n309\t            walk_forward_passers=walk_forward_pass,\n310\t            simplicity_passers=ratchet_pass,\n311\t            recommended=ratchet_pass[0] if ratchet_pass else None,\n312\t            rationale=await self._generate_rationale(candidate, mutations, results),\n313\t        )\n314\t        await self.report_repo.save(report)\n315\t        await self._notify_user_for_review(report)\n316\t        return report\n317\t```\n318\t\n319\t### UC-2: Evaluate Mutation on Historical Period\n320\t\n321\t```python\n322\tclass EvalRunner:\n323\t    \"\"\"Run pipeline with mutation against historical period, compute metrics.\"\"\"\n324\t\n325\t    async def run(self, mutation: Mutation, period: EvalPeriod) -> EvalResult:\n326\t        # Temporary pipeline instance with mutation applied\n327\t        pipeline = self.pipeline_factory.create(config_override=mutation.config_diff)\n328\t\n329\t        # Get eval thesis set for period (hold-out, not used for training)\n330\t        thesis_eval = await self.eval_set_repo.get_thesis_eval(period, holdout=True)\n331\t        kol_eval = await self.eval_set_repo.get_kol_eval(period, holdout=True)\n332\t        pump_eval = await self.eval_set_repo.get_pump_eval(period, holdout=True)\n333\t\n334\t        # Run pipeline on eval inputs, compare to known outcomes\n335\t        thesis_scores = []\n336\t        for thesis_input in thesis_eval:\n337\t            predicted = await pipeline.validate_thesis(thesis_input.ticker, as_of=thesis_input.as_of)\n338\t            thesis_scores.append(self._score_thesis(predicted, thesis_input.known_outcome))\n339\t\n340\t        # Similarly for alerts, pumps, KOL calibration...\n341\t        metrics = Metrics(\n342\t            thesis_hit_rate=mean([s.hit for s in thesis_scores]),\n343\t            thesis_excess_return=mean([s.excess_return for s in thesis_scores]),\n344\t            alert_precision=self._compute_alert_precision(pipeline, period, holdout=True),\n345\t            alert_recall=self._compute_alert_recall(pipeline, period, holdout=True),\n346\t            pump_detection_f1=self._compute_pump_f1(pipeline, pump_eval),\n347\t            kol_calibration_convergence=self._compute_kol_convergence(pipeline, kol_eval),\n348\t            simplicity_penalty=self._complexity_penalty(mutation),\n349\t        )\n350\t\n351\t        composite = self._compute_composite(metrics)\n352\t        return EvalResult(\n353\t            mutation_id=mutation.id, period=period, metrics=metrics, composite=composite,\n354\t        )\n355\t```\n356\t\n357\t### UC-3: Apply Approved Mutation to Production\n358\t\n359\t```python\n360\tclass ApproveAndDeployMutation:\n361\t    \"\"\"Human has approved a proposed mutation. Apply to production config.\"\"\"\n362\t\n363\t    async def execute(self, report_id: str, mutation_id: str, human_approver: str) -> DeployedChange:\n364\t        report = await self.report_repo.get(report_id)\n365\t        mutation = next(m for m in report.mutations_tested if m.id == mutation_id)\n366\t\n367\t        # Version current production\n368\t        current_version = await self.git_service.tag_current_state(\n369\t            tag=f\"pipeline-v{self.current_version + 1}-pre-mutation\"\n370\t        )\n371\t\n372\t        # Apply mutation to config file\n373\t        await self.config_service.apply_mutation(mutation)\n374\t\n375\t        # Tag new version\n376\t        new_version_tag = await self.git_service.tag_current_state(\n377\t            tag=f\"pipeline-v{self.current_version + 2}\"\n378\t        )\n379\t\n380\t        deployed = DeployedChange(\n381\t            change_id=new_id(),\n382\t            report_id=report_id,\n383\t            mutation_id=mutation_id,\n384\t            approved_by=human_approver,\n385\t            deployed_at=datetime.utcnow(),\n386\t            pre_mutation_version=current_version,\n387\t            post_mutation_version=new_version_tag,\n388\t            monitoring_window_days=28,\n389\t            rollback_threshold_metric_drop=0.20,\n390\t        )\n391\t        await self.deployed_changes_repo.save(deployed)\n392\t        await self._start_monitoring(deployed)\n393\t        return deployed\n394\t```\n395\t\n396\t### UC-4: Monitor & Auto-Rollback\n397\t\n398\t```python\n399\tclass RegressionMonitor:\n400\t    \"\"\"Daily: check deployed changes for regression. Auto-rollback if >20% drop.\"\"\"\n401\t\n402\t    async def check_deployed_changes(self):\n403\t        active_changes = await self.deployed_changes_repo.get_active_monitoring()\n404\t        for change in active_changes:\n405\t            if (datetime.utcnow() - change.deployed_at).days > change.monitoring_window_days:\n406\t                change.status = MONITORING_COMPLETE\n407\t                await self.deployed_changes_repo.save(change)\n408\t                continue\n409\t\n410\t            current_metric = await self.metrics_service.compute_recent(window_days=7)\n411\t            baseline = change.pre_mutation_baseline_metric\n412\t            drop_pct = (baseline - current_metric) / baseline\n413\t\n414\t            if drop_pct > change.rollback_threshold_metric_drop:\n415\t                await self._auto_rollback(change, reason=f\"metric_dropped_{drop_pct:.1%}\")\n416\t                await self.event_bus.publish(ChangeRolledBack(change.change_id, drop_pct))\n417\t```\n418\t\n419\t## B.4 Mutation Generator\n420\t\n421\tThe mutation generator is itself LLM-assisted. Claude proposes variants to an editable asset. Example:\n422\t\n423\t```python\n424\tclass MutationGenerator:\n425\t    \"\"\"LLM-assisted mutation generation for editable assets.\"\"\"\n426\t\n427\t    async def generate(self, asset: EditableAsset, n_variants: int, constraint: str) -> list[Mutation]:\n428\t        if asset.mutation_types == [\"numeric_range\"]:\n429\t            # Simple: random perturbations within defined range\n430\t            return self._generate_numeric_variants(asset, n_variants)\n431\t        elif asset.mutation_types == [\"prompt_variant\"]:\n432\t            # Complex: LLM proposes prompt rewrites\n433\t            return await self._generate_prompt_variants(asset, n_variants)\n434\t        elif asset.mutation_types == [\"rule_addition\", \"rule_removal\"]:\n435\t            return await self._generate_rule_variants(asset, n_variants)\n436\t        # ...\n437\t\n438\t    async def _generate_prompt_variants(self, asset: EditableAsset, n: int) -> list[Mutation]:\n439\t        \"\"\"LLM proposes variations of a prompt, with rationale for each.\"\"\"\n440\t        current_prompt = await self._read_asset(asset)\n441\t        recent_failures = await self._recent_failures_relevant_to(asset)\n442\t\n443\t        prompt = f\"\"\"\n444\tYou are proposing variants of this LLM system prompt for an investment analysis agent.\n445\t\n446\tCurrent prompt:\n447\t{current_prompt}\n448\t\n449\tRecent failure modes observed:\n450\t{recent_failures}\n451\t\n452\tGenerate {n} variants. Each variant:\n453\t- Must preserve core role/purpose\n454\t- Should address one specific observed failure mode\n455\t- Rationale must be explicit (why this change might improve quality)\n456\t- Minimize length change — unnecessary verbosity is penalized\n457\t\n458\tOutput JSON array of {{variant_id, new_prompt, rationale, expected_improvement_area}}.\n459\t\"\"\"\n460\t        response = await self.llm.complete(prompt)\n461\t        return self._parse_prompt_variants(response)\n462\t```\n463\t\n464\t## B.5 Eval Set Management\n465\t\n466\t```python\n467\t# eval-sets/ directory structure\n468\t\n469\teval-sets/\n470\t├── historical-theses/\n471\t│   ├── 2023-H1/\n472\t│   │   ├── holdout/         # 30% — NEVER used for training\n473\t│   │   │   ├── hpg-2023-02-15.json   # ticker, as_of_date, known_outcome\n474\t│   │   │   └── ...\n475\t│   │   └── training/        # 70% — can be used for prompt refinement\n476\t│   ├── 2023-H2/\n477\t│   └── ...\n478\t├── labeled-pumps/\n479\t│   ├── 2022-flc-cycle.yaml\n480\t│   ├── 2023-thep-rally.yaml\n481\t│   └── ...\n482\t├── labeled-kol-recommendations/\n483\t│   ├── calibration-set.json\n484\t│   └── holdout-set.json\n485\t├── known-value-traps/\n486\t└── known-winners/\n487\t```\n488\t\n489\tEach eval item has:\n490\t- Input context (ticker, as_of_date)\n491\t- Known outcome (return at 3m/6m/12m, labels)\n492\t- Metadata (when labeled, by whom, confidence in label)\n493\t\n494\t## B.6 Database Schema\n495\t\n496\t```sql\n497\t-- db/migrations/009_outer_loop.sql\n498\t\n499\tCREATE TABLE optimization_reports (\n500\t    report_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n501\t    week_of DATE NOT NULL,\n502\t    candidate_asset TEXT NOT NULL,\n503\t    baseline_score REAL NOT NULL,\n504\t    mutations_tested JSONB NOT NULL,\n505\t    walk_forward_passers TEXT[],\n506\t    simplicity_passers TEXT[],\n507\t    recommended TEXT,\n508\t    rationale TEXT NOT NULL,\n509\t    status TEXT NOT NULL,\n510\t    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n511\t    reviewed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,\n512\t    reviewer TEXT,\n513\t    review_decision TEXT,\n514\t    review_notes TEXT\n515\t);\n516\t\n517\tCREATE TABLE deployed_changes (\n518\t    change_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n519\t    report_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES optimization_reports(report_id),\n520\t    mutation_id TEXT NOT NULL,\n521\t    approved_by TEXT NOT NULL,\n522\t    deployed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,\n523\t    pre_mutation_version TEXT NOT NULL,\n524\t    post_mutation_version TEXT NOT NULL,\n525\t    pre_mutation_baseline_metric REAL NOT NULL,\n526\t    monitoring_window_days INT NOT NULL,\n527\t    rollback_threshold_metric_drop REAL NOT NULL,\n528\t    status TEXT NOT NULL,            -- monitoring | complete | rolled_back\n529\t    rolled_back_at TIMESTAMPTZ,\n530\t    rollback_reason TEXT\n531\t);\n532\t\n533\tCREATE TABLE eval_runs (\n534\t    run_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n535\t    mutation_id TEXT NOT NULL,\n536\t    eval_period_start DATE NOT NULL,\n537\t    eval_period_end DATE NOT NULL,\n538\t    metrics JSONB NOT NULL,\n539\t    composite REAL NOT NULL,\n540\t    duration_ms INT NOT NULL,\n541\t    ran_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()\n542\t);\n543\t```\n544\t\n545\t## B.7 Cadences\n546\t\n547\t- **Weekly optimization run**: Sunday 02:00\n548\t- **User review of report**: within 7 days (or auto-expires, no action = reject)\n549\t- **Deployment of approved**: following Monday 06:00\n550\t- **Monitoring of deployed**: daily 23:00 for 28 days\n551\t- **Auto-rollback check**: daily 23:30 for any change in monitoring\n552\t- **Quarterly eval set refresh**: first Sunday of quarter\n553\t\n554\t## B.8 Tasks (Year 2 Phase)\n555\t\n556\t**Phase 1** (infrastructure, ~4 weeks):\n557\t- Editable asset registry + mutation framework\n558\t- Eval set loader + partitioner (train/holdout)\n559\t- Metric computation service\n560\t- Composite scoring formula\n561\t\n562\t**Phase 2** (mutation generators, ~3 weeks):\n563\t- Numeric variant generator\n564\t- Prompt variant generator (LLM-assisted)\n565\t- Rule variant generator\n566\t- Validation of proposed mutations\n567\t\n568\t**Phase 3** (evaluation, ~4 weeks):\n569\t- Walk-forward eval runner\n570\t- Historical pipeline replay\n571\t- Metric aggregation\n572\t- Report generation\n573\t\n574\t**Phase 4** (deployment + monitoring, ~3 weeks):\n575\t- Git-tag-based versioning\n576\t- Approval workflow UI\n577\t- Regression monitor + auto-rollback\n578\t- Change archive browser\n579\t\n580\t## B.9 Risks & Mitigations\n581\t\n582\t| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |\n583\t|---|---|---|---|\n584\t| Goodhart: optimize metric, harm real performance | HIGH | CRITICAL | Hold-out set, multi-metric, walk-forward, human review |\n585\t| Overfitting to historical regime | HIGH | HIGH | Walk-forward validation + quarterly eval refresh |\n586\t| LLM proposes broken mutations | MEDIUM | MEDIUM | Mutation validator + dry-run before full eval |\n587\t| User rubber-stamps approval | MEDIUM | HIGH | Reviewer must write rationale for accept; spot-checked by agent critic |\n588\t| Rollback triggers too often | LOW | MEDIUM | Threshold tunable; 20% is starting point |\n589\t| Accumulated changes make system incomprehensible | MEDIUM | HIGH | Simplicity penalty + quarterly \"what's the current state?\" review |\n590\t\n591\t---\n592\t\n593\t# PART C — PROVENANCE & REVIEW\n594\t\n595\t## C.1 Why This Design\n596\t\n597\t**Considered alternative: full autonomous pipeline evolution**\n598\t- Rejected: too dangerous without 2+ years of calibration. Goodhart risk too high.\n599\t\n600\t**Considered alternative: no outer loop, manual iteration forever**\n601\t- Rejected: doesn't leverage the Karpathy insight; compounds slower than system should.\n602\t\n603\t**Considered alternative: Year 1 activation with limited assets**\n604\t- Rejected: insufficient eval data leads to overfitting noise.\n605\t\n606\t**Considered alternative: single composite metric**\n607\t- Accepted with modification: composite IS used, but computed from multi-metric basis, not single number.\n608\t\n609\t## C.2 Open Questions\n610\t\n611\t- Who should be trusted to approve changes? If project gains users, does each user have their own outer loop?\n612\t- How to handle market regime shifts (post-2024 regime may invalidate 2022 eval data)?\n613\t- Can outer loop propose changes to itself (meta-meta optimization)? Probably not Year 2.\n614\t- When does outer loop get to touch Python code (not just configs/prompts)?\n615\t\n616\t## C.3 Reviews\n617\t\n618\t| Date | Reviewer | Status | Notes |\n619\t|---|---|---|---|\n620\t| 2026-04-23 | project-owner | Approved | Initial |\n621\t"}]},"uuid":"bf9a3143-cee8-415b-a5dd-d08a653573d7","timestamp":"2026-05-09T12:03:29.859Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\specs\\tier2-feature\\005-karpathy-outer-loop.md","content":"---\nspec_id: SPEC-2026-04-23-005\ntier: 2\nstatus: approved\nversion: 1.0\ncreated: 2026-04-23\nauthors: [project-owner]\nbounded_contexts: [Analysis, Calibration, Market Data]\nrelated_specs: [SPEC-2026-04-23-T1-001, SPEC-2026-04-23-004]\nubiquitous_language_terms: [Outer Loop, Editable Asset, Scalar Metric, Eval Set, Goodhart's Law, Ratchet, Simplicity Criterion, Meta-Optimization, Walk-Forward]\n---\n\n# SPEC: Karpathy Outer Loop — Pipeline Self-Optimization (Year 2)\n\n> Applies the Karpathy autoresearch pattern to optimize signal weights, prompts, and rules over time.\n> **This spec activates in Year 2.** Year 1 is calibration-data-accumulation; without sufficient data, outer loop has nothing to optimize against.\n\n---\n\n# PART A — BUSINESS SPECIFICATION\n\n## A.1 Context\n\nKarpathy's autoresearch loop: LLM agent edits an `editable_asset` repeatedly, each edit evaluated by a `scalar_metric`, within a `time_boxed_cycle`. Best results kept (ratchet), simpler solutions preferred (simplicity criterion).\n\nApplied to StockForge: **we don't optimize investment decisions directly** (that's Goodhart trap — LLM would learn to hack whatever metric we use). We optimize the **pipeline** that produces investment theses.\n\n**Editable assets**:\n- Signal weights in confluence engine\n- Prompt templates for perspective agents\n- Pump phase classifier thresholds\n- KOL credibility formula parameters\n- Narrative phase transition rules\n- Screening rules in watchlist\n\n**Scalar metrics** (on HOLD-OUT set, not used for tuning):\n- Thesis hit rate (primary)\n- Alert precision/recall\n- Pump detection precision/recall\n- KOL calibration CI width\n\n**Time-boxed cycle**: each \"experiment\" = re-run pipeline on historical period + measure metric, ~1-2 hours.\n\n## A.2 Why Year 2 Activation\n\nKarpathy loop requires **evaluation data**. StockForge generates evaluation data through:\n- Thesis outcomes (3-12 month review cycle)\n- KOL recommendation outcomes (1-12 month cycle)\n- Pump detection outcomes (30-90 days post-detection)\n- Narrative phase predictions vs actual phase evolution\n\n**Minimum eval set sizes before outer loop meaningful**:\n- 100+ completed thesis with outcomes\n- 500+ KOL recommendations with outcomes\n- 20+ labeled historical pumps with outcomes\n- 10+ narratives through full lifecycle\n\nThese take ~12-18 months to accumulate. Running outer loop with insufficient data = overfit to noise, worse than doing nothing.\n\n## A.3 The Goodhart Problem\n\nThe #1 risk: outer loop optimizes for the metric, not for real-world value. Mitigations:\n\n**M-1 Hold-Out Test Set** — 30% of evaluation data never seen by outer loop. Final metric always computed on hold-out. If training metric improves but hold-out degrades: reject.\n\n**M-2 Multi-Metric Composite** — never optimize single metric. Composite of thesis_hit_rate + alert_precision + calibration_accuracy + simplicity_penalty.\n\n**M-3 Simplicity Ratchet** — if edit adds complexity (more rules, more parameters, longer prompt) but improves metric marginally (<5% lift), reject.\n\n**M-4 Walk-Forward Validation** — each proposed change tested on 3 non-overlapping historical windows. Must improve in ≥2 of 3 to be accepted.\n\n**M-5 Human Review of Proposed Changes** — outer loop proposes; human approves before production. Not autonomous in year 2.\n\n**M-6 Eval Set Rotation** — eval set refreshes quarterly (new data added, oldest retired). Prevents pipeline from memorizing specific eval items.\n\n## A.4 Three Loops Recap\n\n**Outer loop (this spec, weekly cycle, Year 2+)** — meta-optimization: edit pipeline params + prompts + rules\n\n**Middle loop (continuous, Phase 1+)** — ingestion: hourly news, daily KOL, scheduled reviews, live data\n\n**Inner loop (per-query, Phase 1+)** — thesis validation: ticker → 6 perspectives → synthesis\n\nEach loop has different cadence, different editable assets, different metrics.\n\n## A.5 Core Use Cases\n\n**UC-1 Weekly Optimization Run** — Every Sunday: outer loop picks one editable asset from candidate list, proposes N variations, runs each through eval pipeline, ranks by composite metric, produces report.\n\n**UC-2 Human Review & Accept** — User reviews weekly report. Approves, rejects, or requests modification. Approved changes go to production next week.\n\n**UC-3 Regression Alert** — If a change in production causes metric to drop >20% over 4 weeks, auto-rollback to prior version + flag for investigation.\n\n**UC-4 Proposal Archive** — All proposed changes (accepted or rejected) archived with full rationale + results. Pattern: what tends to work, what tends to fail.\n\n**UC-5 Manual Experiment Request** — User can propose specific experiment (\"try reducing KOL weight 20%\"), outer loop runs it through same eval pipeline.\n\n## A.6 Business Rules\n\n**BR-1 Never Auto-Deploy** — outer loop PROPOSES, human ACCEPTS. Year 2 at minimum. Maybe never fully autonomous.\n\n**BR-2 Eval Set Never Used for Training** — strict separation. Eval set lives in `eval-sets/`; training data for prompt refinement lives elsewhere.\n\n**BR-3 Multi-Metric Composite** — no single-metric optimization. Composite defined in `configs/outer-loop-metrics.yaml`.\n\n**BR-4 Simplicity Preferred** — complexity penalty in composite. New rule adds score iff |improvement| > complexity_cost.\n\n**BR-5 Walk-Forward Mandatory** — propose change → test on 3 non-overlapping windows → accept if 2+ improve.\n\n**BR-6 Rollback Trigger Automated** — metric drops >20% in 4 weeks of production = automatic revert to previous version, manual re-review required.\n\n**BR-7 Changes Versioned** — every pipeline version is a git tag. Rollback = git checkout.\n\n**BR-8 Proposals Limited Per Week** — max 3 proposals per week to prevent noise. Forces thoughtful selection.\n\n**BR-9 Prompt Changes Human-Reviewed First** — no automated prompt editing in year 2. All prompt changes reviewed line-by-line before testing.\n\n**BR-10 Minimum Eval Set Enforced** — outer loop refuses to run if eval set below minimums (see A.2).\n\n## A.7 Success Criteria (Year 2)\n\n**Month 15** (activation + 3 months):\n- Outer loop runs weekly, produces reports\n- ≥5 proposals reviewed, ≥2 accepted\n- Documented cases: metric improvement from specific changes\n\n**Month 18**:\n- Accepted changes show compounding improvement (metric lift from baseline)\n- No auto-rollback triggered (changes were sound)\n- Human review time <30 min/week\n\n**Month 24**:\n- Outer loop has produced ≥20 accepted changes\n- Pipeline metric improved ≥30% vs baseline\n- Changes in \"pattern library\" (what kinds of changes work)\n\n**Qualitative**:\n- I trust the proposals enough that review feels valuable, not performative\n- Outer loop caught at least one case where my intuition was wrong\n- Pipeline demonstrably smarter than when we started\n\n## A.8 Out of Scope\n\n- Autonomous code changes (outer loop proposes to config + prompts, not Python code)\n- Optimizing individual perspective prompts (BR-9 restriction)\n- Year 1 activation (insufficient data)\n- Multi-user tenancy (single user Year 2)\n\n---\n\n# PART B — AGENT CONTRACT\n\n## B.1 Editable Asset Registry\n\n```yaml\n# configs/outer-loop/editable-assets.yaml\n\neditable_assets:\n  - id: confluence_weights\n    path: configs/signals/confluence-weights.yaml\n    description: How much each tier contributes to confluence score\n    mutation_types: [numeric_range, numeric_relative]\n    safety: high  # changes immediately affect alerts\n\n  - id: pump_classifier_thresholds\n    path: configs/signals/pump-classifier.yaml\n    description: Thresholds for pump phase classification\n    mutation_types: [numeric_range]\n    safety: high\n\n  - id: kol_credibility_formula\n    path: configs/calibration/kol-credibility.yaml\n    description: Bayesian prior + decay + sector weighting\n    mutation_types: [numeric_range, formula_variant]\n    safety: medium  # affects scoring but calibration is statistical\n\n  - id: narrative_phase_thresholds\n    path: configs/signals/narrative-phases.yaml\n    description: Thresholds for INCUBATION → EMERGING etc transitions\n    mutation_types: [numeric_range]\n    safety: medium\n\n  - id: screening_rules\n    path: configs/screeners/*.yaml\n    description: Watchlist screening rule variants\n    mutation_types: [rule_addition, rule_removal, threshold_change]\n    safety: low  # easy to revert\n\n  - id: synthesizer_prompt\n    path: prompts/analysis/synthesizer.md\n    description: System prompt for synthesizer\n    mutation_types: [prompt_variant]\n    safety: high  # affects all thesis output\n    human_review_required: line_by_line\n\n  - id: perspective_prompts\n    path: prompts/analysis/perspectives/*.md\n    description: System prompts for 6 perspective agents\n    mutation_types: [prompt_variant]\n    safety: high\n    human_review_required: line_by_line\n```\n\n## B.2 Metrics Definition\n\n```yaml\n# configs/outer-loop/metrics.yaml\n\ncomposite_metric:\n  weights:\n    thesis_hit_rate: 0.35         # primary\n    thesis_excess_return: 0.20    # beats benchmark\n    alert_precision: 0.15         # not crying wolf\n    alert_recall: 0.10            # not missing opportunities\n    pump_detection_f1: 0.10\n    kol_calibration_convergence: 0.05\n    simplicity_penalty: -0.05     # subtracted\n\n  normalization:\n    # Each sub-metric normalized to [0, 1] based on historical distribution\n\n  simplicity_penalty:\n    formula: |\n      lines_of_rules_added * 0.01\n      + prompt_tokens_added * 0.001\n      + new_parameters * 0.05\n\nmetric_calculation:\n  eval_periods:\n    - start: 2023-01-01\n      end: 2023-06-30\n    - start: 2023-07-01\n      end: 2023-12-31\n    - start: 2024-01-01\n      end: 2024-06-30\n    - start: 2024-07-01\n      end: 2024-12-31\n\n  min_thesis_per_period: 20       # won't run if fewer\n  min_kol_recs_per_period: 100\n  min_pump_cases_per_period: 5\n```\n\n## B.3 Core Use Cases\n\n### UC-1: Weekly Optimization Run\n\n```python\n# apps/analyst-agents/outer_loop/weekly_runner.py\n\nclass WeeklyOptimizationRunner:\n    \"\"\"Every Sunday: pick candidate → generate mutations → evaluate → report.\"\"\"\n\n    async def execute(self) -> OptimizationReport:\n        # Step 0: Check minimum eval set sizes\n        if not await self._eval_set_minimums_met():\n            return OptimizationReport(status=SKIPPED, reason=\"insufficient_eval_data\")\n\n        # Step 1: Pick candidate editable asset (LLM-assisted)\n        candidates = await self.asset_registry.get_candidates()\n        # Prioritize: assets not recently modified, assets where metric drift observed\n        candidate = await self.candidate_selector.select(candidates, self.recent_history)\n\n        # Step 2: Generate mutations (3-5 variants)\n        mutations = await self.mutation_generator.generate(\n            asset=candidate,\n            n_variants=4,\n            constraint=candidate.safety_level,\n        )\n\n        # Step 3: Run each mutation through eval pipeline (walk-forward)\n        results = []\n        for mutation in [current_baseline] + mutations:\n            for eval_period in self.config.eval_periods:\n                result = await self.eval_runner.run(mutation, eval_period)\n                results.append((mutation, eval_period, result))\n\n        # Step 4: Aggregate walk-forward scores\n        scores_by_mutation = {}\n        for mutation, period, result in results:\n            scores_by_mutation.setdefault(mutation.id, []).append(result)\n\n        walk_forward_pass = []\n        for mut_id, period_results in scores_by_mutation.items():\n            # Must improve in ≥2 of 3 periods\n            baseline = scores_by_mutation[CURRENT_BASELINE_ID]\n            improvements = sum(\n                1 for mut_res, base_res in zip(period_results, baseline)\n                if mut_res.composite > base_res.composite\n            )\n            if improvements >= 2 and mut_id != CURRENT_BASELINE_ID:\n                walk_forward_pass.append(mut_id)\n\n        # Step 5: Apply simplicity ratchet\n        ratchet_pass = []\n        for mut_id in walk_forward_pass:\n            mutation = next(m for m in mutations if m.id == mut_id)\n            if mutation.complexity_delta < 0 or (\n                self._avg_improvement(mut_id) > mutation.complexity_delta * 0.05\n            ):\n                ratchet_pass.append(mut_id)\n\n        # Step 6: Generate report\n        report = OptimizationReport(\n            week=self.current_week,\n            candidate_asset=candidate.id,\n            baseline_score=self._score(CURRENT_BASELINE_ID),\n            mutations_tested=len(mutations),\n            walk_forward_passers=walk_forward_pass,\n            simplicity_passers=ratchet_pass,\n            recommended=ratchet_pass[0] if ratchet_pass else None,\n            rationale=await self._generate_rationale(candidate, mutations, results),\n        )\n        await self.report_repo.save(report)\n        await self._notify_user_for_review(report)\n        return report\n```\n\n### UC-2: Evaluate Mutation on Historical Period\n\n```python\nclass EvalRunner:\n    \"\"\"Run pipeline with mutation against historical period, compute metrics.\"\"\"\n\n    async def run(self, mutation: Mutation, period: EvalPeriod) -> EvalResult:\n        # Temporary pipeline instance with mutation applied\n        pipeline = self.pipeline_factory.create(config_override=mutation.config_diff)\n\n        # Get eval thesis set for period (hold-out, not used for training)\n        thesis_eval = await self.eval_set_repo.get_thesis_eval(period, holdout=True)\n        kol_eval = await self.eval_set_repo.get_kol_eval(period, holdout=True)\n        pump_eval = await self.eval_set_repo.get_pump_eval(period, holdout=True)\n\n        # Run pipeline on eval inputs, compare to known outcomes\n        thesis_scores = []\n        for thesis_input in thesis_eval:\n            predicted = await pipeline.validate_thesis(thesis_input.ticker, as_of=thesis_input.as_of)\n            thesis_scores.append(self._score_thesis(predicted, thesis_input.known_outcome))\n\n        # Similarly for alerts, pumps, KOL calibration...\n        metrics = Metrics(\n            thesis_hit_rate=mean([s.hit for s in thesis_scores]),\n            thesis_excess_return=mean([s.excess_return for s in thesis_scores]),\n            alert_precision=self._compute_alert_precision(pipeline, period, holdout=True),\n            alert_recall=self._compute_alert_recall(pipeline, period, holdout=True),\n            pump_detection_f1=self._compute_pump_f1(pipeline, pump_eval),\n            kol_calibration_convergence=self._compute_kol_convergence(pipeline, kol_eval),\n            simplicity_penalty=self._complexity_penalty(mutation),\n        )\n\n        composite = self._compute_composite(metrics)\n        return EvalResult(\n            mutation_id=mutation.id, period=period, metrics=metrics, composite=composite,\n        )\n```\n\n### UC-3: Apply Approved Mutation to Production\n\n```python\nclass ApproveAndDeployMutation:\n    \"\"\"Human has approved a proposed mutation. Apply to production config.\"\"\"\n\n    async def execute(self, report_id: str, mutation_id: str, human_approver: str) -> DeployedChange:\n        report = await self.report_repo.get(report_id)\n        mutation = next(m for m in report.mutations_tested if m.id == mutation_id)\n\n        # Version current production\n        current_version = await self.git_service.tag_current_state(\n            tag=f\"pipeline-v{self.current_version + 1}-pre-mutation\"\n        )\n\n        # Apply mutation to config file\n        await self.config_service.apply_mutation(mutation)\n\n        # Tag new version\n        new_version_tag = await self.git_service.tag_current_state(\n            tag=f\"pipeline-v{self.current_version + 2}\"\n        )\n\n        deployed = DeployedChange(\n            change_id=new_id(),\n            report_id=report_id,\n            mutation_id=mutation_id,\n            approved_by=human_approver,\n            deployed_at=datetime.utcnow(),\n            pre_mutation_version=current_version,\n            post_mutation_version=new_version_tag,\n            monitoring_window_days=28,\n            rollback_threshold_metric_drop=0.20,\n        )\n        await self.deployed_changes_repo.save(deployed)\n        await self._start_monitoring(deployed)\n        return deployed\n```\n\n### UC-4: Monitor & Auto-Rollback\n\n```python\nclass RegressionMonitor:\n    \"\"\"Daily: check deployed changes for regression. Auto-rollback if >20% drop.\"\"\"\n\n    async def check_deployed_changes(self):\n        active_changes = await self.deployed_changes_repo.get_active_monitoring()\n        for change in active_changes:\n            if (datetime.utcnow() - change.deployed_at).days > change.monitoring_window_days:\n                change.status = MONITORING_COMPLETE\n                await self.deployed_changes_repo.save(change)\n                continue\n\n            current_metric = await self.metrics_service.compute_recent(window_days=7)\n            baseline = change.pre_mutation_baseline_metric\n            drop_pct = (baseline - current_metric) / baseline\n\n            if drop_pct > change.rollback_threshold_metric_drop:\n                await self._auto_rollback(change, reason=f\"metric_dropped_{drop_pct:.1%}\")\n                await self.event_bus.publish(ChangeRolledBack(change.change_id, drop_pct))\n```\n\n## B.4 Mutation Generator\n\nThe mutation generator is itself LLM-assisted. Claude proposes variants to an editable asset. Example:\n\n```python\nclass MutationGenerator:\n    \"\"\"LLM-assisted mutation generation for editable assets.\"\"\"\n\n    async def generate(self, asset: EditableAsset, n_variants: int, constraint: str) -> list[Mutation]:\n        if asset.mutation_types == [\"numeric_range\"]:\n            # Simple: random perturbations within defined range\n            return self._generate_numeric_variants(asset, n_variants)\n        elif asset.mutation_types == [\"prompt_variant\"]:\n            # Complex: LLM proposes prompt rewrites\n            return await self._generate_prompt_variants(asset, n_variants)\n        elif asset.mutation_types == [\"rule_addition\", \"rule_removal\"]:\n            return await self._generate_rule_variants(asset, n_variants)\n        # ...\n\n    async def _generate_prompt_variants(self, asset: EditableAsset, n: int) -> list[Mutation]:\n        \"\"\"LLM proposes variations of a prompt, with rationale for each.\"\"\"\n        current_prompt = await self._read_asset(asset)\n        recent_failures = await self._recent_failures_relevant_to(asset)\n\n        prompt = f\"\"\"\nYou are proposing variants of this LLM system prompt for an investment analysis agent.\n\nCurrent prompt:\n{current_prompt}\n\nRecent failure modes observed:\n{recent_failures}\n\nGenerate {n} variants. Each variant:\n- Must preserve core role/purpose\n- Should address one specific observed failure mode\n- Rationale must be explicit (why this change might improve quality)\n- Minimize length change — unnecessary verbosity is penalized\n\nOutput JSON array of {{variant_id, new_prompt, rationale, expected_improvement_area}}.\n\"\"\"\n        response = await self.llm.complete(prompt)\n        return self._parse_prompt_variants(response)\n```\n\n## B.5 Eval Set Management\n\n```python\n# eval-sets/ directory structure\n\neval-sets/\n├── historical-theses/\n│   ├── 2023-H1/\n│   │   ├── holdout/         # 30% — NEVER used for training\n│   │   │   ├── hpg-2023-02-15.json   # ticker, as_of_date, known_outcome\n│   │   │   └── ...\n│   │   └── training/        # 70% — can be used for prompt refinement\n│   ├── 2023-H2/\n│   └── ...\n├── labeled-pumps/\n│   ├── 2022-flc-cycle.yaml\n│   ├── 2023-thep-rally.yaml\n│   └── ...\n├── labeled-kol-recommendations/\n│   ├── calibration-set.json\n│   └── holdout-set.json\n├── known-value-traps/\n└── known-winners/\n```\n\nEach eval item has:\n- Input context (ticker, as_of_date)\n- Known outcome (return at 3m/6m/12m, labels)\n- Metadata (when labeled, by whom, confidence in label)\n\n## B.6 Database Schema\n\n```sql\n-- db/migrations/009_outer_loop.sql\n\nCREATE TABLE optimization_reports (\n    report_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n    week_of DATE NOT NULL,\n    candidate_asset TEXT NOT NULL,\n    baseline_score REAL NOT NULL,\n    mutations_tested JSONB NOT NULL,\n    walk_forward_passers TEXT[],\n    simplicity_passers TEXT[],\n    recommended TEXT,\n    rationale TEXT NOT NULL,\n    status TEXT NOT NULL,\n    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n    reviewed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,\n    reviewer TEXT,\n    review_decision TEXT,\n    review_notes TEXT\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE deployed_changes (\n    change_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n    report_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES optimization_reports(report_id),\n    mutation_id TEXT NOT NULL,\n    approved_by TEXT NOT NULL,\n    deployed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,\n    pre_mutation_version TEXT NOT NULL,\n    post_mutation_version TEXT NOT NULL,\n    pre_mutation_baseline_metric REAL NOT NULL,\n    monitoring_window_days INT NOT NULL,\n    rollback_threshold_metric_drop REAL NOT NULL,\n    status TEXT NOT NULL,            -- monitoring | complete | rolled_back\n    rolled_back_at TIMESTAMPTZ,\n    rollback_reason TEXT\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE eval_runs (\n    run_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n    mutation_id TEXT NOT NULL,\n    eval_period_start DATE NOT NULL,\n    eval_period_end DATE NOT NULL,\n    metrics JSONB NOT NULL,\n    composite REAL NOT NULL,\n    duration_ms INT NOT NULL,\n    ran_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n```\n\n## B.7 Cadences\n\n- **Weekly optimization run**: Sunday 02:00\n- **User review of report**: within 7 days (or auto-expires, no action = reject)\n- **Deployment of approved**: following Monday 06:00\n- **Monitoring of deployed**: daily 23:00 for 28 days\n- **Auto-rollback check**: daily 23:30 for any change in monitoring\n- **Quarterly eval set refresh**: first Sunday of quarter\n\n## B.8 Tasks (Year 2 Phase)\n\n**Phase 1** (infrastructure, ~4 weeks):\n- Editable asset registry + mutation framework\n- Eval set loader + partitioner (train/holdout)\n- Metric computation service\n- Composite scoring formula\n\n**Phase 2** (mutation generators, ~3 weeks):\n- Numeric variant generator\n- Prompt variant generator (LLM-assisted)\n- Rule variant generator\n- Validation of proposed mutations\n\n**Phase 3** (evaluation, ~4 weeks):\n- Walk-forward eval runner\n- Historical pipeline replay\n- Metric aggregation\n- Report generation\n\n**Phase 4** (deployment + monitoring, ~3 weeks):\n- Git-tag-based versioning\n- Approval workflow UI\n- Regression monitor + auto-rollback\n- Change archive browser\n\n## B.9 Risks & Mitigations\n\n| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Goodhart: optimize metric, harm real performance | HIGH | CRITICAL | Hold-out set, multi-metric, walk-forward, human review |\n| Overfitting to historical regime | HIGH | HIGH | Walk-forward validation + quarterly eval refresh |\n| LLM proposes broken mutations | MEDIUM | MEDIUM | Mutation validator + dry-run before full eval |\n| User rubber-stamps approval | MEDIUM | HIGH | Reviewer must write rationale for accept; spot-checked by agent critic |\n| Rollback triggers too often | LOW | MEDIUM | Threshold tunable; 20% is starting point |\n| Accumulated changes make system incomprehensible | MEDIUM | HIGH | Simplicity penalty + quarterly \"what's the current state?\" review |\n\n---\n\n# PART C — PROVENANCE & REVIEW\n\n## C.1 Why This Design\n\n**Considered alternative: full autonomous pipeline evolution**\n- Rejected: too dangerous without 2+ years of calibration. Goodhart risk too high.\n\n**Considered alternative: no outer loop, manual iteration forever**\n- Rejected: doesn't leverage the Karpathy insight; compounds slower than system should.\n\n**Considered alternative: Year 1 activation with limited assets**\n- Rejected: insufficient eval data leads to overfitting noise.\n\n**Considered alternative: single composite metric**\n- Accepted with modification: composite IS used, but computed from multi-metric basis, not single number.\n\n## C.2 Open Questions\n\n- Who should be trusted to approve changes? If project gains users, does each user have their own outer loop?\n- How to handle market regime shifts (post-2024 regime may invalidate 2022 eval data)?\n- Can outer loop propose changes to itself (meta-meta optimization)? Probably not Year 2.\n- When does outer loop get to touch Python code (not just configs/prompts)?\n\n## C.3 Reviews\n\n| Date | Reviewer | Status | Notes |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 2026-04-23 | project-owner | Approved | Initial |\n","numLines":621,"startLine":1,"totalLines":621}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"b4421f4a-e118-40b0-a581-cba5b55e439e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"142a2b14-79c6-486b-8a85-0887f39d14e4","version":"2.1.126","gitBranch":"main"}

import dataclass\nfrom datetime import UTC, datetime\n\nfrom scipy.stats import beta as _scipy_beta\n\nfrom packages.domain.influence.models.credibility_score import CredibilityScore\nfrom packages.domain.influence.models.outcome_review import (\n    OutcomeReview,\n    OutcomeStatus,\n)\nfrom packages.domain.influence.models.recommendation import Recommendation\nfrom packages.domain.influence.value_objects.kol_id import KolId\nfrom packages.domain.influence.value_objects.recommendation_id import RecommendationId\nfrom packages.domain.influence.value_objects.sector_score import SectorScore\nfrom packages.domain.influence.value_objects.timeframe import Timeframe\nfrom packages.domain.influence.value_objects.timeframe_score import TimeframeScore\n\n__all__ = [\"CalibrationResult\", \"CalibrationService\"]\n\n\n# Spec § B.3 UC-3: skeptical Beta(5, 5) prior — weakly informative, mean=0.5,\n# dampens small-sample swings (n=3 cannot drive posterior to 1.0).\n_PRIOR_ALPHA = 5.0\n_PRIOR_BETA = 5.0\n\n# Spec § B.1 CredibilityScore: 90% credibility interval (5th + 95th pct).\n_CI_LOWER_QUANTILE = 0.05\n_CI_UPPER_QUANTILE = 0.95\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)\nclass CalibrationResult:\n    \"\"\"Side-channel snapshot of the raw counts used for credibility computation.\n\n    Useful for tests + audit logs that want to see the buckets separately from\n    the posterior aggregate.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    n_evaluated: int\n    n_hits: int\n    n_misses: int\n    n_partial: int\n    n_invalid: int\n    n_inconclusive: int\n\n\nclass CalibrationService:\n    \"\"\"Stateless deterministic Bayesian credibility computer.\n\n    Methods take fully-resolved domain objects + return a new CredibilityScore\n    aggregate. Persistence is the caller's responsibility (see UC-3 use case).\n\n    The scipy.stats.beta dependency is the ONLY external dep; no LLM imports.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def compute(\n        self,\n        *,\n        kol_id: KolId,\n        reviews: list[OutcomeReview],\n        recommendations_by_id: dict[RecommendationId, Recommendation] | None = None,\n        sectors_by_recommendation: dict[RecommendationId, str] | None = None,\n        as_of: datetime | None = None,\n    ) -> CredibilityScore:\n        \"\"\"Compute the posterior credibility for one KOL from their reviews.\n\n        Args:\n            kol_id: KOL whose credibility is being computed.\n            reviews: ALL completed OutcomeReview rows for this KOL.\n            recommendations_by_id: optional {RecommendationId -> Recommendation}\n                map used for per-timeframe disaggregation. When omitted the\n                returned score has empty timeframe_scores.\n            sectors_by_recommendation: optional {RecommendationId -> sector_code}\n                map used for per-sector disaggregation. When omitted the\n                returned score has empty sector_scores.\n            as_of: timestamp for last_updated_at; defaults to now(UTC).\n\n        Returns:\n            CredibilityScore aggregate. Cold-start (0 reviews) yields the prior\n            mean of 0.5 with a wide CI.\n        \"\"\"\n        counts = self._bucket(reviews)\n        post_alpha, post_beta = self._posterior(counts)\n        mean = post_alpha / (post_alpha + post_beta)\n        ci_low = float(_scipy_beta.ppf(_CI_LOWER_QUANTILE, post_alpha, post_beta))\n        ci_high = float(_scipy_beta.ppf(_CI_UPPER_QUANTILE, post_alpha, post_beta))\n\n        timeframe_scores: dict[Timeframe, TimeframeScore] = {}\n        sector_scores: dict[str, SectorScore] = {}\n        if recommendations_by_id:\n            timeframe_scores = self._compute_timeframe_scores(\n                reviews, recommendations_by_id\n            )\n        if sectors_by_recommendation:\n            sector_scores = self._compute_sector_scores(\n                reviews, sectors_by_recommendation\n            )\n\n        return CredibilityScore(\n            kol_id=kol_id,\n            n_evaluated=counts.n_evaluated,\n            n_hits=counts.n_hits,\n            n_misses=counts.n_misses,\n            n_partial=counts.n_partial,\n            posterior_alpha=post_alpha,\n            posterior_beta=post_beta,\n            bayesian_mean=mean,\n            bayesian_ci_low=ci_low,\n            bayesian_ci_high=ci_high,\n            sector_scores=sector_scores,\n            timeframe_scores=timeframe_scores,\n            last_updated_at=as_of if as_of is not None else datetime.now(UTC),\n        )\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _bucket(reviews: list[OutcomeReview]) -> CalibrationResult:\n        n_hits = sum(1 for r in reviews if r.status == OutcomeStatus.HIT)\n        n_misses = sum(1 for r in reviews if r.status == OutcomeStatus.MISS)\n        n_partial = sum(1 for r in reviews if r.status == OutcomeStatus.PARTIAL)\n        n_invalid = sum(1 for r in reviews if r.status == OutcomeStatus.INVALID)\n        n_inconclusive = sum(\n            1 for r in reviews if r.status == OutcomeStatus.INCONCLUSIVE\n        )\n        return CalibrationResult(\n            n_evaluated=len(reviews),\n            n_hits=n_hits,\n            n_misses=n_misses,\n            n_partial=n_partial,\n            n_invalid=n_invalid,\n            n_inconclusive=n_inconclusive,\n        )\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _posterior(counts: CalibrationResult) -> tuple[float, float]:\n        n_total_weighted = counts.n_hits + counts.n_misses + counts.n_partial\n        n_success_weighted = counts.n_hits + 0.5 * counts.n_partial\n        post_alpha = _PRIOR_ALPHA + n_success_weighted\n        post_beta = _PRIOR_BETA + (n_total_weighted - n_success_weighted)\n        return post_alpha, post_beta\n\n    def _compute_timeframe_scores(\n        self,\n        reviews: list[OutcomeReview],\n        recommendations_by_id: dict[RecommendationId, Recommendation],\n    ) -> dict[Timeframe, TimeframeScore]:\n        groups: dict[Timeframe, list[OutcomeReview]] = defaultdict(list)\n        for r in reviews:\n            rec = recommendations_by_id.get(r.recommendation_id)\n            if rec is None:\n                continue\n            groups[rec.timeframe].append(r)\n        result: dict[Timeframe, TimeframeScore] = {}\n        for tf, tf_reviews in groups.items():\n            counts = self._bucket(tf_reviews)\n            alpha, beta_param = self._posterior(counts)\n            mean = alpha / (alpha + beta_param)\n            result[tf] = TimeframeScore(\n                timeframe=tf,\n                n_evaluated=counts.n_evaluated,\n                hit_rate_mean=mean,\n            )\n        return result\n\n    def _compute_sector_scores(\n        self,\n        reviews: list[OutcomeReview],\n EvalKind\n\n__all__ = [\"DEFAULT_MINIMUMS\", \"Year2ActivationGate\"]\n\n\n# Spec 005 § A.2 — minimum eval set sizes before outer loop is meaningful.\nDEFAULT_MINIMUMS: dict[EvalKind, int] = {\n
